scenes.tts: How does the width of the midline between the folds affect whether they can meet? A simple cartoon shows the idea.
scenes.visual: Title card: Where in the Plate? A cross-section with two raised folds and a midline strip; a question mark over the midline width.
scenes.narration: How does the width of the midline between the folds affect whether they can meet? A simple cartoon shows the idea.

scenes.tts: Put your hands flat, thumbs touching, and roll each up onto its thumb edge. The top edges meet, however broad your hands.
scenes.visual: Two hands flat on a table, thumbs touching; they roll up on their thumb edges and meet at the little-finger edges. Broader hands shown in outline: they still meet.
scenes.narration: Put your hands flat, thumbs touching, and roll each up onto its thumb edge. The top edges meet, however broad your hands.

scenes.tts: Now put a book between your thumbs. Upright, the hands stop apart by the book's width.
scenes.visual: A book between the thumbs; upright hands stand apart by the book's width.
scenes.narration: Now put a book between your thumbs. Upright, the hands stop apart by the book's width.

scenes.tts: Broader hands do not help unless you tip them past upright. The book is the midline.
scenes.visual: Broader hands still apart. The book relabels as midline; the hands as neural folds. Label: a cartoon, the real midline creases at a hinge.
scenes.narration: Broader hands do not help unless you tip them past upright. The book is the midline.

scenes.tts: How does the midline narrow? Cells crawl in between their side neighbours. This is intercalation.
scenes.visual: A grid of cells; cells slip between their side neighbours. Label: intercalation.
scenes.narration: How does the midline narrow? Cells crawl in between their side neighbours. This is intercalation.

scenes.tts: Same cells, rearranged: narrower across, longer along. This is convergent extension.
scenes.visual: On screen: 40 cells across by 50 long becomes 20 across by 100 long. Same 2,000 cells. Label: idealized, no cell division. Label: convergent extension, converge across, extend along.
scenes.narration: Same cells, rearranged: narrower across, longer along. This is convergent extension.

scenes.tts: But which way is across? On a fly's wing, every hair points toward the tip. In mutant flies, the hairs swirl.
scenes.visual: Wing hairs all pointing to the wingtip; then, labelled frizzled or Van Gogh mutant, the hairs swirl.
scenes.narration: But which way is across? On a fly's wing, every hair points toward the tip. In mutant flies, the hairs swirl.

scenes.tts: Frizzled and Dishevelled gather on one side of each cell. Van Go and Prickle gather on the other.
scenes.caption: Frizzled and Dishevelled gather on one side of each cell. Van Gogh and Prickle gather on the other.
scenes.visual: One wing cell enlarged: Frizzled and Dishevelled coloured on one side; Van Gogh and Prickle on the opposite side.
scenes.narration: Frizzled and Dishevelled gather on one side of each cell. Van Gogh and Prickle gather on the other.

scenes.tts: This is planar cell polarity, a sense of direction within a sheet.
scenes.visual: Label: planar cell polarity (PCP). Arrows across the neural plate grid all agree on side to side.
scenes.narration: This is planar cell polarity, a sense of direction within a sheet.

scenes.tts: In two thousand two, John Wallingford and Richard Harland asked where in the frog plate it matters.
scenes.caption: In 2002, John Wallingford and Richard Harland asked where in the frog plate it matters.
scenes.visual: Credit: Wallingford and Harland, 2002. A frog embryo, Xenopus laevis.
scenes.narration: In 2002, John Wallingford and Richard Harland asked where in the frog plate it matters.

scenes.tts: Frog cell fates are mapped, so an injection can be aimed at one part of the plate.
scenes.visual: An early embryo with one cell injected; its descendants light up a known region of the neural plate.
scenes.narration: Frog cell fates are mapped, so an injection can be aimed at one part of the plate.

scenes.tts: They injected a Dishevelled built to block planar polarity. In some embryos it reached the midline; in others, the sides.
scenes.visual: Two embryos: one with the midline tinted blue, one with the sides tinted orange. Label: Dishevelled blocked here.
scenes.narration: They injected a Dishevelled built to block planar polarity. In some embryos it reached the midline; in others, the sides.

scenes.tts: Predict. Which embryos keep an open tube: those blocked at the midline, or those blocked at the sides?
scenes.visual: Pause card: Predict. Which embryo stays open? An empty table: where blocked, plate width, folds rise, tube closes.
scenes.narration: Predict. Which embryos keep an open tube: those blocked at the midline, or those blocked at the sides?

scenes.tts: Blocked at the midline, the plate stayed wide. The folds rose and moved inward. But the tube stayed open.
scenes.visual: Table row fills: midline, stays wide, yes, no. The blue embryo's folds rise but stay apart.
scenes.narration: Blocked at the midline, the plate stayed wide. The folds rose and moved inward. But the tube stayed open.

scenes.tts: Blocked at the sides, where the folds form and fuse, closure was normal.
scenes.visual: Table row fills: sides, width not reported, yes (closure was normal), yes. The orange embryo's tube closes.
scenes.narration: Blocked at the sides, where the folds form and fuse, closure was normal.

scenes.tts: The hands rose with the book still between them. Dishevelled is needed at the midline.
scenes.visual: The hands and book cartoon beside the blue embryo. Caption: Dishevelled is needed at the midline.
scenes.narration: The hands rose with the book still between them. Dishevelled is needed at the midline.

scenes.tts: A mouse points the same way. The loop-tail mouse carries a mutation in Vangle two, a relative of Van Go.
scenes.caption: A mouse points the same way. The loop-tail mouse carries a mutation in Vangl2, a relative of Van Gogh.
scenes.visual: A loop-tail mouse with a kinked tail (one copy). Gene label: Vangl2, mouse relative of fly Van Gogh.
scenes.narration: A mouse points the same way. The loop-tail mouse carries a mutation in Vangl2, a relative of Van Gogh.

scenes.tts: With two copies, the tube is open from the midbrain down the spine.
scenes.visual: Two-copy embryo: the flat map open from the midbrain to the lower end, labelled craniorachischisis.
scenes.narration: With two copies, the tube is open from the midbrain down the spine.

scenes.tts: In two thousand seven, Andrew Copp's laboratory labelled that midline. Before neurulation began, it had failed to extend.
scenes.caption: In 2007, Andrew Copp's laboratory labelled that midline. Before neurulation began, it had failed to extend.
scenes.visual: Credit: Copp laboratory, 2007. A labelled midline that has failed to extend.
scenes.narration: In 2007, Andrew Copp's laboratory labelled that midline. Before neurulation began, it had failed to extend.

scenes.tts: And Closure one never happened.
scenes.caption: And Closure 1 never happened.
scenes.visual: The Closure 1 site marked with a cross.
scenes.narration: And Closure 1 never happened.

scenes.tts: Narrowing starts early and overlaps folding. The plate must still bend, and the fold tips must stick together.
scenes.visual: Cross-section: hinge points crease while the midline is still narrowing; fold tips meet and adhere. Caption: narrowing is not the whole job.
scenes.narration: Narrowing starts early and overlaps folding. The plate must still bend, and the fold tips must stick together.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: the midline must be narrow enough for the folds to close the gap. Frog and mouse both tie closure to midline narrowing.
scenes.visual: Closing card: narrow enough, then fold. Frog, Dishevelled at the midline; mouse, Vangl2.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: the midline must be narrow enough for the folds to close the gap. Frog and mouse both tie closure to midline narrowing.
